properties.decision: UNSETTLED. Six things are mechanically decidable and none is currently reported: (1) is anything under `.reflow2/` tracked by git; (2) are the MCP configs tracked, carrying absolute paths meaningless on another machine; (3) does `.reflow2/kit-version.json` match the installed kit; (4) do local skill copies exist and differ from the served ones, given a local copy silently SHADOWS the served one; (5) is `--graph-path` absolute rather than relative-and-cwd-dependent; (6) is a committed export present, and current against the live graph. SHAPES, not a recommendation: (a) extend `reflow2_init.py --check`, which already reports what a run would change and already owns the stamp and the skill mirrors — smallest, and it means one command answers "what would change" and "what is wrong"; (b) a separate `reflow2_doctor.py` beside `reflow2_check.py`, on the argument that "would this install change files" and "is this project's reflow2 setup sane" are different questions with different audiences; (c) fold the checks into `check_kit_manifest.py`, which already compares the stamp and is closest in spirit; (d) decline, and put the six checks in a served skill instead, on the ground that an agent can run git itself and instructions are cheaper than code. WHATEVER THE SHAPE, IT REPORTS AND DOES NOT REPAIR: `git rm --cached` is a judgement about someone's history, and rewriting an MCP config is not something to do silently. Name the finding, name the remedy, let the human run it — the same split `dec:ask-not-repair` draws for merges. AND IT CANNOT BE AN MCP TOOL: `dec:agent-navigates-content` keeps reflow2 out of file IO, and every check above reads the filesystem or shells to git. The kit is the home; the machinery is half-built there already.
properties.name: OPEN — should the kit ship a command that tells a project how it is out of date, instead of every agent re-deriving the migration?
properties.rationale: Raised because the evidence arrived in an unusually clean form. `req:thin-install` is ACCEPTED and quotes Alex asking for exactly this on 2026-07-25; `cap:skills-served` delivered the forward half; and on 2026-08-08 Alex — the requirement's own author — spent eight manual steps escaping a 0.11.0 kit under a 0.24.0 binary, because nothing exists for a project installed BEFORE served skills. TWO AGENTS DERIVED THAT MIGRATION INDEPENDENTLY THE SAME DAY AND DISAGREED: his eight steps against my seven, overlapping on six. His included a regression (rewriting `--graph-path` to a relative path, the configuration `dec:no-design-here-never-looked` records as minting an accidental third graph in Anthony's own repo); mine got the stamp filename wrong on first pass. Neither was careless — the knowledge is scattered across the installer source, three accepted decisions and two verifications, and is re-derived per session. That is the failure reflow2's own instructions name as its reason to exist, pointed at the migration rather than the design. Evidence: fact:defect-a-pre-served-skills-install-is-stranded and fact:defect-installer-cannot-warn-that-the-graph-dir-is-already-tracked.
